removalReason: The artifact's PROVENANCE is a production database read, and a production read-back does not belong in the repository as committed content regardless of what its rows happen to contain.

Its row values were seeded test data -- every one of the 190 partIds carried the `TST-` prefix, originating from the synthetic catalog that `field-ops-app-vite/src/data/partsCatalog.ts` documents itself as generated from. So this removal is provenance hygiene, not a customer-data incident.

The claims the audit actually cites from this file are structural -- field coverage, row count, the `NOT_EXPOSED_IN_SOURCE` marking -- and every one of them is preserved below. No cited conclusion depended on a row value.

fieldCoverage.note: `internalPartNumber` and `category` were marked NOT_EXPOSED_IN_SOURCE for all 190 rows. That is the fact `evidence-review.md` §2.1 and `part-identity-evidence.md` cite; it is a property of the read projection, not of any record.

identifierShape.note: Recorded because it is the evidence for the classification above. No identifier values are reproduced here.

hashNote: Already published in this directory's SHA256SUMS.txt before removal, so recording it here discloses nothing new and keeps the evidence chain verifiable against any copy an operator holds.

aiIngestion.reason: docs/audits/** is excluded by the Keystone repository-intelligence content policy (intelligence/eos_repository_policy.json). The exclusion was applied to the git tree LISTING, so the file's bytes were never read.

historyNote: Removing the file from the tree does not remove it from git history; the blob remains reachable at earlier commits. A history rewrite is destructive and coordinated, and is an Owner decision rather than something this change performs.
